completion.content: LoRA stands for Low-Rank Adaptation. It fine-tunes a model using small trainable low-rank matrices while keeping the original model weights frozen.
QLoRA combines low-rank adapters with a frozen quantized base model, typically using 4-bit weights, to reduce GPU memory requirements during fine-tuning.

prompt.content: What is the purpose of an attention mechanism?

completion.content: Attention allows a transformer to weight information from different token positions when computing contextual representations.
Tokenization converts text into token identifiers that a language model can process. Tokens may represent words, subwords, characters, or other text units.

Gradient accumulation combines gradients across multiple smaller batches before updating model parameters, allowing a larger effective batch size without holding every example in GPU memory simultaneously.

prompt.content: How does LoRA differ from full fine-tuning?

completion.content: Full fine-tuning updates all selected model parameters, whereas LoRA freezes the pretrained base weights and trains a much smaller set of low-rank adapter parameters.
